routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.approach: Typically reached after climbing the North Face or Hanging Glacier route to the upper mountain, or via the NW Rib between the White Salmon and Hanging Glaciers.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.approach: From Marblemount on WA-20, drive the Cascade River Road (FR-15) about 19-21 miles (paved to roughly mile 10, then gravel/washboard) to the Eldorado trailhead (~2,150 ft). Cross the North Fork Cascade River and follow the unmaintained Eldorado climbers' trail through forest and a boulder field to treeline, then to Eldorado Basin/Roush Creek camps (~6,000-6,300 ft). routes.descent: Downclimb the ridge crest back around The Smokestack via its west-side gully, return to the Klawatti-Austera Col, then to Klawatti Col. From there re-cross the Inspiration Glacier to the notch on Eldorado's East Ridge, descend the Eldorado Glacier, a

routes.name: Avalanche Glacier
routes.description: A steeper, more direct way to the summit of Mount Adams than the popular South Spur, climbing straight up the Avalanche Glacier through some moderate ice sections.
routes.approach: From Cold Springs trailhead, traverse via round-the-mountain trail to the southwest side of Mount Adams, approach glacier directly from southwest.
routes.descent: From the summit, descend south via the South Spur snowfields (or the snowfield adjacent to the Avalanche/White Salmon glaciers) back toward the Morrison Creek/Cold Springs approach, glissading where conditions allow.

routes.name: Avalanche-White Salmon Glaciers
routes.approach: Start at the Cold Springs trailhead (about 5,600 ft) at the end of FR 8040 and walk the South Climb Trail up the old roadbed to its junction with the Round the Mountain Trail near 6,200 ft. Turn right (northwest) onto the Round the Mountain Trail and follow its up-and-down traverse for roughly two miles, much of it under snow in early season, to the stream draining the Avalanche Glacier basin near
routes.descent: Climb out onto the summit plateau and head for the true summit, then descend the South Spur: cross the crater rim past Pikers Peak and follow the broad snow slopes of Crescent Ridge down to the Lunch Counter flats, where glissading is common on soft

routes.name: North Ridge (West Face)
routes.approach: Start at the Killen Creek trailhead on FR 2329 north of Takhlakh Lake and follow Killen Creek Trail 113 south for about 3.2 miles through lodgepole forest and meadows to the Pacific Crest Trail junction near 6,100 ft. routes.descent: Descend the North Ridge, also called the North Cleaver, back toward High Camp. This is a walk-off over loose volcanic scree and boulders and is longer than it looks from above, with a real chance of knocking rock onto parties below, so spread out and

routes.name: Pinnacle Glacier Headwall
routes.approach: A free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead. From the Riley Camp Trailhead, hike the Riley Camp Trail, staying off the Riley Cut-Off at the first junction, until it meets the Pacific Crest Trail. Turn south on the Pacific Crest Trail for a few minutes to Riley Creek and follow the creek up through boulders to the moraines at the foot of the Pinnacle Glacier. The headwall route begins

routes.name: Coleman Ski Descent
routes.approach: Start at the Heliotrope Ridge trailhead (about 3,700 ft) at the end of Glacier Creek Road (FR 39) and follow Trail 677 through old growth, crossing several creeks that run higher in the afternoon than the morning. routes.descent: Ski or walk off by the way you came up. From the summit plateau drop down the Roman Wall, a snow slope of 35 to 45 degrees that is usually downclimbed or skied with care when it is icy, onto the Deming Glacier. Cross the saddle and ski the Coleman Gl

routes.name: Southeast Chute
routes.approach: Start at the Upper Trailhead (about 3,500 ft) at the end of the spur off FS 24, which needs a Northwest Forest Pass. Trail 812 climbs at once, with stacked switchbacks for the first 0.3 mile before it merges with the lower-trailhead trail near 3,900 ft. routes.descent: Descend the chute you climbed. When the snow is continuous, most parties glissade it with an axe in hand, losing roughly 1,000 ft quickly; only do so in control, because a fall on firm or icy snow, or exposed rocks and ice bulges lower down, can inju

routes.name: Pika Slab
routes.approach: From I-5 exit 208 head east 4 miles on Highway 530 to Arlington, then continue east on SR 530 for 28 miles to Darrington. At the four-way intersection in town turn right onto the Mountain Loop Highway and follow paved then graveled road for roughly 12.5-14 miles to a prominent Mount Pugh sign, where FR 2095 branches off on the left. FR 2095 is narrow, one-lane and unpaved; drive it about 1.5 miles

routes.name: Mount Si Trail
routes.approach: From Seattle, take I-90 east to Exit 32 (436th Ave SE). Turn left and go north on 436th Ave SE to its end at SE North Bend Way. Turn left, and after 0.3 mi turn right onto SE Mt. Si Road. Follow it 2.4 mi to the large trailhead lot on the left. The trail starts at the lot. Keep left at the Talus Loop junction at about 0.7 mi, and continue past Snag Flats (about 2 mi) to Haystack Basin (about 4 mi)
routes.descent: Go back down the main trail the way you came up. The descent is steep and unrelenting, and it is hard on the knees. Trekking poles help. In the shoulder seasons, the upper trail above Snag Flats can hold packed snow or ice when the trailhead is warm

routes.name: Lynch Glacier
routes.approach: From the Deception Pass Trailhead, hike to Marmot/Jade Lakes, continue to Dip Top Gap, then traverse west to the shoulder overlooking the Foss River drainage and descend to the outlet of Pea Soup Lake.

routes.name: Southeast Route
routes.approach: Park at the Necklace Valley (East Fork Foss) trailhead at the end of FR 68 and follow the East Fork Foss trail up the valley. The first five miles are gentle forest, gaining only about 600 ft, until a footlog crossing of the East Fork Foss River, then the trail climbs about 2,400 ft in three miles of steep, rooty switchbacks to Jade Lake and on up the Necklace Valley past the other lakes. routes.descent: Reverse the ridge to La Bohn Lakes. The rock on the ridge is loose, with blocks that shift underfoot, so test holds and keep clear of other parties. From the lakes, drop back to Necklace Valley either by the heather and cairn line along the tree line

routes.name: West Route
routes.approach: From the Necklace Valley Trailhead, follow the Necklace Valley Trail up the East Fork Foss River, over the river crossing and the steep climb beyond it, to the hanging valley holding La Bohn Lakes, where parties camp. From the lakes, climb the snow chute or talus to La Bohn Gap; the climb proper heads due north from the gap toward the summit.
